clue.text: Ursa Minor seen west of a Caribbean island

parts.note: Ursa Minor is the Little Bear, and a little bear is a cub
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stargazer locates the Little Bear constellation over the sea west of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen west of' puts CUB to the left of A in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest island of the Greater Antilles, lying in the Caribbean Sea south of Florida.

clue.text: Modern kind of scanner to search around a burial site

indicators.note: around means the first pieces go round the next one

parts.note: a CAT scanner is a computerised medical imaging device
to comb is to search thoroughly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Archaeologists use modern scanning equipment to search a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: A CAT scan is computerised tomography; 'Modern' marks it as recent technology rather than a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground cemetery of tunnels with recesses for tombs, as in ancient Rome.

clue.text: In African country, preserve ancient tribe

indicators.note: in means the next piece is put inside the country

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: A West African nation conserves an old tribal people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserve' looks like a verb about keeping a tribe going; it is the noun jam.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from Jacob's youngest son.

clue.text: Origin of conflict — abuses, perhaps, turning bad?

definitions.text: Origin of conflict — abuses, perhaps, turning bad?

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so its first letter is taken
perhaps suggests the letters of abuses could be arranged some other way
turning means the word for bad is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: bad means ill, as in feeling bad

explanation.surface: A question whether mistreatment souring into hostility is what starts a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the abuses into ASUSBE, and 'turning' reverses the word for bad. Read whole, the clue describes a provocation to war.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for an occasion of war: an act or event that provokes or justifies hostilities.

clue.text: A shrub planted round front of garden in row

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: planted round means the shrub is set around the next letter

parts.note: rue is a bitter aromatic shrub

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bush has been planted around the edge of a garden in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line of plants, but it is a quarrel, rhyming with cow.
explanation.definitionFit: To row is to quarrel noisily, a verb meaning dispute or bicker.

clue.text: Engaged in doing drug, fully informed

parts.note: up to means busy with, as in what are you up to
speed is slang for amphetamine

explanation.surface: Someone busy taking drugs claims to know everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning well briefed and aware of the latest developments.

clue.text: In which one heavenly body eclipses others

definitions.text: In which one heavenly body eclipses others

parts.words: In which one heavenly body eclipses others
parts.note: reads like astronomy, but a heavenly body is a gorgeous figure outshining rivals in a pageant

explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' looks like a star or planet; it means a gorgeous figure, and 'eclipses' means outshines.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant judging looks, where one gorgeous entrant outshines the rest.

clue.text: Long and tedious series showed up a city in US

parts.note: lit up means illuminated, made visible
taken as written
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Someone appeared for a long boring list of complaints in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer form of repeated petitions, extended to any tediously repeated list.

clue.text: Deflated, flat like this? Absolutely!

parts.note: the word deflated is the word flat put inside the word deed

explanation.surface: Someone agrees emphatically that a tyre has gone down.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split in two, IN DEED, says where 'flat' sits in DEFLATED: DE + FLAT + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic adverb of agreement, a synonym for certainly or truly.

clue.text: Wine and spirits a guy can get attached to

definitions.text: a guy can get attached to

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, used for communion
a peg is a measure of spirits, especially in old Anglo-Indian usage

explanation.surface: Someone says wine and spirits are things a fellow can grow fond of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' is not a man but a guy rope, the line that holds a tent up and is tied off on a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes of a camping shelter are tied to these stakes driven into the ground.

clue.text: One needing MP's backing

parts.note: the head of government needs support from members of parliament; also the letters MP turned back give that leader's abbreviation

explanation.walkthrough: Doubly cryptic: a government leader needs MPs' support, and 'backing' MP gives PM.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a parliamentary government, who must keep the confidence of the House.

clue.text: Tried eating duck cooked in one way

indicators.note: eating means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to try food is to taste it
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A diner sampled duck that had been prepared a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the dish but is the zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Browned by dry heat under a grill, which is one particular method of cooking bread.

clue.text: Recitals composed to include new instruments

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters take the next piece inside
composed means put together, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Concert performances are written to feature some newly made instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges RECITALS, and 'to include' puts N inside that arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-reed woodwinds played in orchestras and bands are examples of musical instruments.

clue.text: Present, possibly, but not together?

definitions.meaning: the present is one grammatical form of a verb, with past and future
together in slang means calm and composed, so not together means uptight and nervous

explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the grammar term. 'Together' is the informal sense of self-possessed.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical category of verbs such as present or past; also nervously strained, the opposite of composed.

clue.text: Penning one is each MP's need, originally

definitions.text: Penning one is each MP's need, originally

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
originally hints at an inventive, fresh arrangement of the letters just before it

parts.note: taken as written, the S included
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Writing a first address to the Commons is something every new Member of Parliament must do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' is an anagram signal here, not 'first letters'. Read whole, the clue describes what each newly elected MP must deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: A new Member of Parliament's first address to the House, which every newcomer must give.

clue.text: Tiny lead horse had, frantically covering last part of straight

indicators.note: covering means the rearranged letters go round the next letter
frantically suggests wild disorder, so these letters are rearranged
the last part of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A racehorse's slender advantage was frantically defended along the home straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny lead' is a racing margin, not a small leash; 'frantically' is the anagram signal and 'covering' puts the T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, the smallest winning margin, less than a head's length.

clue.text: Musical craft in a quartet, say, led by piano

indicators.note: led by means the piano letter goes in front

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
taken as written

indicators.note: say means the word is heard as it is spoken

parts.note: a quartet is a group of four

explanation.surface: A boat in a musical has a quartet of singers, accompanied by piano.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera named after a ship. 'say' turns FOUR into FORE.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Pinafore, a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, is named after its fictional ship, so a vessel from a musical.

clue.text: OK? Better than just OK

definitions.meaning: as a reply, all right then, agreeing

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the reluctant 'fine'; the other is literally very plus well.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase of grudging assent, and also an intensified form of good health or skill.

clue.text: Drink of rum I order in vain

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries in vain to order a glass of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink being ordered, but it is the adjective meaning odd, which rearranges I ORDER IN VAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: French for ordinary wine: cheap table wine is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Engraved, say, without excessive ornamentation

indicators.note: say means the word is heard when spoken out

parts.note: metal that is chased has been engraved with a design

explanation.surface: Engraving, they say, should avoid too much decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: In style, pure and simple, unadorned by fussy decoration.

clue.text: Various seabirds

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning several or sundry
birds of the loon family, called loons in North America

explanation.walkthrough: The birds are loons; the adjective is an archaic word for sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for several or sundry; also the British name for loons, diving waterbirds.

clue.text: Greeting covers small island and part of large one

indicators.note: covers means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames

explanation.surface: A welcome extends over a little isle and part of a bigger one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'island' earlier: the answer shares a large island, Hispaniola, with the Dominican Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean nation occupies the western third of Hispaniola, a much larger island.

clue.text: Going by air, a distant part of Ireland'

definitions.text: Going by air, a distant part of Ireland

parts.words: Going by air, a distant part of Ireland
parts.note: an air is a tune, and by the famous First World War marching song, this Irish county is a long way to go

explanation.walkthrough: 'Going by air' looks like flying; an air is a tune, the soldiers' song 'It's a Long Way to ...', which names this county.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish county made famous by the wartime song saying it lies a long way off.

clue.text: Briefly visit old man at home

parts.note: pop is an informal name for one's father
in means at home

explanation.surface: A short call on one's father at his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to call in on someone for a short time.

clue.text: Put up with intensive pressure that woman has to bear

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the woman carries the pressure within her

parts.note: she is that woman
heat means intense pressure, as in the heat is on

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates the fierce strain a woman must carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like tolerate, but it is putting a sword up, back in its scabbard.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a sword or knife is to return it to its scabbard or cover.

clue.text: Hollow in road, however, quickly covered by staff

indicators.note: covered by means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a staff is a pole
though, meaning however, written quickly in its short informal spelling

explanation.surface: A dip in the road is hastily covered over with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quickly' shortens 'though' to THO, the informal spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit worn into a road surface by traffic and weather, a depression drivers dread.

clue.text: For example, welcoming Scandinavian girl in Northern area

indicators.note: welcoming means taking inside, so the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
Astrid is a common Scandinavian girl's name

explanation.surface: A northern district, say, warmly receives a young woman from Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer was a division of Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A former administrative division of Yorkshire in the north of England, a region.

clue.text: Wood for split deck

definitions.meaning: pine or fir timber, sawn into planks
to share out a pack of cards among players

explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's floor, which would suit 'Wood'; it is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Softwood timber such as pine or fir; also to distribute playing cards to each player.
